ledger.note: 1525: Albert resigns as Grand Master and founds the Duchy of Prussia as a fief of Poland. 'On 10 April 1525, Albert resigned his position, became a Protestant... secularized the order's prevailing Prussian territory (the Monastic Prussia)', sealed 'by the Prussian Homage in Kraków in April 1525'; status 'Fief of Poland (until 1657)'. The Prussian Homage page adds the place and the overlord: 10 April 1525 at Kraków, to King Sigismund I the Old, and 8 April 1525 for the Treaty of Kraków. The suzerainty over the duchy is for the Polish dossiers (house-of-jagiellon, polish-lithuanian-commonwealth) to carry as vassal_start 1525 / vassal_end 1657.

Infobox ruler list: John Sigismund 1618-1619, but the text says George William was 'successfully invested with the duchy in 1623'. Month from the Margraviate of Brandenburg page (infobox 'Brandenburg-Prussia: 27 August 1618'; 'When Albert Frederick, Duke of Prussia died without a son in 1618'); added by reviewer eu-09-j.

ledger.note: 1618: the Duchy of Prussia passes to Brandenburg-Prussia. Dissolve is the map's reading: the duchy continued as a Polish fief until the 1657 Treaty of Wehlau gave full sovereignty ('full sovereignty over the duchy under the 1657 Treaty of Wehlau, confirmed in the 1660 Treaty of Oliva') and was raised to a kingdom in 1701; Cliopatria draws the land inside Brandenburg-Prussia from 1619. Month 8: Albert Frederick died on 27 August 1618 (Margraviate of Brandenburg page infobox), reviewer eu-09-j.

certainty.note: Neither page opened gives a boundary line; the frontier with Royal Prussia and Warmia on the west and with Poland and Lithuania on the south and east follows Cliopatria's outline. The 1525 homage fixed the duchy's existence, not a surveyed border.

notes: Written by eu-09-j on 2026-10-25 from two pages (budget 1-2). SHAPE: Cliopatria's two shapes (1526-1611, 1612-1618) are the same 165 cells; they are also cell for cell the Teutonic Order's shape of 1521-1525, so the duchy appears as the order's rump after the 1466 loss of western Prussia, secularised in 1525. The shapes include 31 cells of the gazetteer's Warmia region; the Duchy page keeps Warmia (Polish-controlled) and Royal Prussia outside the duchy, so every keyframe subtracts Warmia. WARS: none listed. The Prussian Homage page says the Treaty of Kraków 'officially ended the Polish-Teutonic War on 8 April 1525' but neither page gives the war's start, so no war entry was written (an entry would need a date from memory). For the Polish dossiers: the Duchy was a Polish fief 1525-1657 (vassal_start 1525, vassal_end 1657 by Wehlau); this dossier does not carry the suzerain's side. ENDING: the Duchy lasted as a legal entity to 1701 (kingdom) but Cliopatria's Brandenburg-Prussia row takes over the land in 1619 and contains all of it, so the dossier ends in 1618 to avoid drawing the land twice; the page itself dates the duchy's inheritance by Brandenburg to 1618 and Wehlau sovereignty to 1657. DISAGREEMENT: the page's infobox gives John Sigismund as duke 1618-1619 and George William from 1619, while the text says George William was invested in 1623. COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: teutonic-order (Cliopatria row 1236-1525, in no group's list of mine). Unknown month for the 1618 inheritance (the page gives the year only; the death of Albert Frederick is not dated on the pages opened).
